text: "Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense I now make before you."
When they heard him addressing them in Hebrew, they became even more quiet. Then he said:

"I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia but brought up in this city. I was trained at the feet of Gamaliel in the strict observance of the law of our fathers, and I was zealous for God, just as all of you are today.
I persecuted this Way to the death, arresting both men and women and throwing them into prison,

as the high priest and the whole council of elders can testify. From them I obtained letters to the brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to bring those who were there back to Jerusalem in chains to be punished.
"As I was on my way and nearing Damascus, about noon a brilliant light from heaven suddenly flashed all around me.
I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?'
I answered, 'Who are you, Lord?' And he said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.'
Those who were with me saw the light, but they did not understand the voice of the one who was speaking to me.

versions.text: Those who were with me saw the light, but they did not understand the voice of the one speaking to me.
versions.explanation: The Greek verb here is simply 'heard' (ἤκουσαν); rendering it 'understand' is a defensible harmonization with 9:7, but a brief footnote noting the literal sense ('did not hear') would help readers. The slight rewording also smooths the read-aloud rhythm at the end of the line.

text: So I asked, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Get up and go into Damascus, and there you will be told all that has been appointed for you to do.'
Since I could not see because of the brightness of that light, my companions took me by the hand and led me into Damascus.
"A man named Ananias came to me, a devout observer of the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living there.
He stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight.' And at that very moment I could see him.
Then he said: 'The God of our fathers has chosen you to know his will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear a word from his mouth,
for you will be his witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.
And now, why wait any longer? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on his name.'
"After I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance
and saw him saying to me, 'Hurry, leave Jerusalem at once, because they will not accept your testimony about me.'
And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I went from synagogue to synagogue, imprisoning and beating those who believed in you.

versions.text: I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I went from synagogue to synagogue, imprisoning and beating those who believe in you.
versions.explanation: The surrounding narrative is in past tense ('I went... imprisoning and beating'), so the present 'believe' clashes with the sequence; 'believed' keeps the tense consistent for the listener.

versions.text: I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I went from synagogue to synagogue, imprisoning and beating those who believed in you.
versions.explanation: The Greek opens with κἀγὼ ('and I'), which links Paul's reply to the Lord's command in the previous verse. Restoring the connective 'And' helps a listener hear the exchange as a dialogue rather than an isolated statement. The existing rendering is defensible, since English narrative often drops such connectives.

text: And when the blood of Stephen your witness was shed, I was standing there giving my approval, guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.'
But he said to me, 'Go, for I am sending you far away to the Gentiles.'"
They listened to him until he said this, and then they raised their voices and shouted, "Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!"
As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and flinging dust into the air,
the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks, directing that he be flogged and questioned so that he might find out why the crowd was shouting at him like this.

versions.text: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that he be flogged and interrogated in order to find out why the people were shouting at him like this.
versions.explanation: In the current wording the two pronouns 'He directed that he be flogged' are ambiguous when read aloud (commander vs. Paul). Joining the clauses keeps the Greek's single sentence and clarifies who is acting.

text: But as they were stretching him out to be whipped, Paul said to the centurion standing there, "Is it legal for you to flog a Roman citizen who has not even been condemned?"
When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it. "What are you about to do?" he said. "This man is a Roman citizen."
The commander came and asked him, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes," he answered.
The commander said, "I paid a great deal of money for my citizenship." "But I was born a citizen," Paul replied.
Immediately those who were about to interrogate him withdrew, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

The next day, wanting to know exactly what the Jews were accusing him of, he released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
